hypothesis: For positive constant underestimation and overestimation costs, the outcome-uniform asymmetric absolute-loss harm set is an exact direction-dependent interval, and projecting into its recursively feasible intersection preserves all PCHP online properties.
claimed_exact_supremum: c_over*(p-b) if p>=b; c_under*(b-p) if p<b
information_boundary: Protected baseline and candidate are prefix-causal; outcome y is never used; eta and both costs are positive constants within a trajectory.
implementation_scope: One generalized trajectory operator plus an analytic worst-case-loss-increase function; the original equal-cost PCHP API must remain numerically identical.

gates: Analytic supremum equals direct evaluation over all piecewise-linear breakpoint regions for randomized scalar tuples.
Every point inside the claimed interval satisfies the declared loss budget and points immediately outside violate it for a constructive outcome.
Setting both costs to one reproduces the existing symmetric PCHP output exactly across randomized trajectories.
Generalized outputs are prefix-invariant, non-increasing, within the physical range, and satisfy the asymmetric pointwise budget.
A zero budget returns the protected baseline exactly.
A larger overestimation cost tightens only the upward side of the feasible tube; a larger underestimation cost tightens only the downward side.
Non-positive or non-finite costs, negative or non-finite budgets, increasing baselines, and shape mismatches fail closed.
falsification.pass_rule: All gates pass with tolerance 1e-12 and the existing symmetric test suite remains green.
falsification.failure_rule: Any failed gate yields REJECT; do not add the extension to the manuscript.
